app.title: MARS-OS: Circadian-Kernel (Mission Biological Drift Monitor)
app.summary: The person sets the length of a mission, the day they are on now, a crew member's chronotype and wake time, and how strong the light-therapy correction is. The interface then simulates every day of the mission. It shows the current alert status, the accumulated phase drift, a performance index and a light-exposure window for today, and counts how many days fall in each alert band. Charts plot performance and drift across the whole mission, with a marker on the current day. These can be overlaid with four fixed correction scenarios. A table lists the values for sampled days, and the person can download the full day-by-day projection or the sampled timeline as CSV.

task.text: Project how a circadian clock drifts out of phase across a long mission under a chosen light-therapy level, and get each day's alert level and light prescription.

data.text: A day-by-day projection made by a model from a few settings: phase drift, a performance index, an alert band and a light-exposure prescription for every day. No data is loaded.
data.item: one mission day with its drift, performance index, alert band and light-exposure window

stage.text: planning a countermeasure schedule by simulation, before the mission

mechanism.text: Sidebar sliders and a selector set the model's settings, and every change re-runs the whole simulation. The status badge, metric cards, mission-long line charts (with alert bands and a current-day marker), the prescription panel and the sampled table all redraw from that one run. A checkbox swaps the single run in the charts for four fixed correction scenarios.

field.text: circadian oscillator modelling of phase drift and light-therapy correction in chronobiology

workflow.name: simulate a quantity over time under adjustable settings and export the day-by-day projection

steps.step: set the conditions the model runs under
steps.here: Sliders set mission length in sols, wake time and correction factor (%), and a selector picks the chronotype (early, standard, late). The model re-runs one simulation per day.

steps.step: pick the point in time to read off
steps.here: A 'Current sol' slider, capped at the mission length, sets which day the badge, cards and prescription describe, and moves the dashed marker on the charts.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Cards show accumulated drift in hours, a sigmoid performance index with a bar, today's light window with minutes, lux and wavelength, and how many days fall in each band (GREEN, YELLOW, RED).

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Two line charts plot the performance index and drift over every sol. Shaded bands mark Optimal, Reduced and Critical, and a line marks the critical drift.
A 'Show scenario comparison' checkbox overlays four fixed runs (no intervention, 30%, 60%, full phototherapy) in both charts.
The prescription panel gives wavelength, exposure, the time window in Mars local time, and the phase direction for the current sol. A table lists sampled sols, with the current one highlighted.
Two download buttons save the full per-sol mission report or the sampled timeline as CSV. The report's file name carries the duration and the correction percentage.

distinctive: Drift builds up at a constant rate per day, set by the gap between the environment's day length and the body's clock, and a correction ceiling caps how much of it therapy can remove.
The performance index takes drift modulo a critical threshold, so its curve is sawtooth-shaped rather than a steady decline.
Each day becomes a prescription: an exposure window that shifts with drift, a duration and intensity that scale with it, and a phase direction.
Days are put into three alert bands, and the share of the mission in each band is shown as a stacked bar.

parts.title: Mission, crew and phototherapy settings
parts.summary: Sliders and a selector set mission length, the current day, chronotype, wake time and correction strength, plus a checkbox for the scenario overlay. Every change re-runs the simulation.

parts.title: Current status header
parts.summary: A colour-coded alert badge with today's performance index and settings, beside a large counter for the current day out of the total.

parts.title: Metric cards
parts.summary: Four cards: accumulated drift, the performance index with a bar, today's light-exposure window, and how many days fall in each alert band, shown as a stacked bar.

parts.title: Performance and drift telemetry
parts.summary: Two line charts over the whole mission, one for the performance index and one for accumulated drift, with alert bands, a critical-drift line and a current-day marker. They can show the overlay of four correction scenarios.

parts.title: Light-therapy prescription
parts.summary: An expandable panel with the current day's prescription: wavelength, exposure minutes and lux, the time window in local time, and the phase-shift direction.

parts.title: Sampled mission timeline
parts.summary: A table of sampled days with drift in hours and minutes, the performance index, an alert-band pill and the light window. The current day is highlighted.

parts.title: CSV export
parts.summary: Downloads the full per-day projection, with its settings in the file name, or only the sampled timeline, as CSV.
